points.description: States that a binary search tree is a binary tree (each node has at most two children, left and right).
points.partial_credit: Half credit if it says 'tree' with two children but does not use the term binary tree precisely.

points.description: States the ordering property precisely: for any node, the left child (left subtree) is smaller than the parent.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if the property is stated only loosely, e.g. 'left is smaller' without relating it to the parent node.

points.description: States the ordering property precisely: the parent is smaller than the right child (right subtree), i.e. left < parent < right, holding for every node.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if only the right-side relation is given without saying it applies to every node.

rubric.notes: Full marks need all three elements stated precisely: binary tree, left smaller than parent, parent smaller than right, applying to any node. A vague statement such as 'a sorted tree' or 'used for searching' earns nothing. A wrong ordering (e.g. left larger than parent) loses the point it affects, and confusing it with a plain binary tree or heap earns nothing for the property points.
